steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The central purpose of economic activity is the production of goods and services to satisfy needs (essentials) and wants (desirables).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The three key economic decisions: what to produce, how to produce, and who is to benefit from production.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The three main economic groups are consumers (buy goods/services), producers (make goods/services), and government (regulates and provides public services).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Goods are tangible products (food, clothing); services are intangible (healthcare, education). Both satisfy needs and wants.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between a need and a want, giving two examples of each. | Describe the three key economic decisions that all societies must make. | Analyse how the three main economic groups interact in a market economy.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always define needs vs wants clearly: needs = essentials for survival, wants = desirables beyond survival. When discussing economic groups, show their INTERACTIONS, not just their roles in isolation. Use the 'what, how, for whom' framework whenever discussing economic decisions.
